name: Higgs inflation is a scalar-tensor theory
summary: A large non-minimal coupling ξh²R (ξ~10⁴) makes the SM Higgs the inflaton. Transforming to the Einstein frame flattens the potential into the same plateau as Starobinsky R+R² gravity, giving n_s≈0.965 and r≈0.003 at N≈60.
breaks: The match with Starobinsky R+R² holds only at leading order in the slow-roll plateau; reheating differs. Burgess–Lee–Trott and Barbon–Espinosa argue that the unitarity cutoff ~M_P/ξ undermines the model, and Bezrukov et al. dispute this.

name: Sub-millimetre tests of the inverse-square law
summary: ADD extra dimensions turn Newtonian gravity into a steeper power law below the compactification radius, parametrized as a Yukawa correction; torsion-balance tests of Newton's law below 0.1 mm bound n=2 ADD radii to tens of micrometres.

name: LISA tests first-order electroweak transitions
summary: Electroweak baryogenesis needs a strongly first-order transition, which requires physics beyond the SM since the SM transition is a crossover. Bubble collisions, sound waves and turbulence in such a transition produce a GW background peaking near millihertz, in the LISA band.

name: GR as an effective field theory
summary: Power counting in E/M_Pl makes GR a predictive EFT, as chiral perturbation theory is for pions. The Einstein–Hilbert term is leading and R² terms are suppressed. The long-distance quantum correction to the Newtonian potential (41/10π)Għ/(r²c³) is non-analytic, cutoff-independent and computable (Donoghue; Bjerrum-Bohr, Donoghue and Holstein).

name: Asymptotic safety predicted the Higgs mass
summary: Requiring the SM plus gravity to be asymptotically safe forces the Higgs quartic near zero at the Planck scale, predicting m_h of about 126 GeV with a few-GeV uncertainty two years before the 125 GeV discovery.
breaks: The prediction depends on assumed signs of gravitational anomalous dimensions; it is the same boundary condition as near-criticality of the SM vacuum and is not unique to asymptotic safety.

name: Higgs vacuum metastability in curved spacetime
summary: With m_h=125 GeV and m_t=173 GeV the Higgs quartic runs negative near 1e10-1e11 GeV, so the electroweak vacuum is metastable; gravitational corrections to the bounce (Coleman-De Luccia) and Higgs fluctuations during inflation decide whether our vacuum survives.

name: String theory born from hadron Regge trajectories
summary: The Veneziano amplitude was invented to fit linearly rising Regge trajectories of mesons; reinterpreted as vibrating strings, it predicted a massless spin-2 state that became the graviton once QCD took over the strong interaction.

name: Large-N planar diagrams equal string genus expansion
summary: In 't Hooft's large-N limit, SU(N) Feynman diagrams organize by the genus of the surface they tile, weighted N^(2-2g). This has the form of closed-string perturbation theory with g_s ~ 1/N and is the structural root of gauge/string duality.
breaks: The match goes beyond form only when an explicit dual is known (e.g. AdS/CFT for N=4 SYM). For QCD (N=3, non-conformal) no string dual is known, and 1/N corrections are not small.

name: Particles as unitary irreps of the Poincare group
summary: Wigner's classification defines an elementary particle as an irreducible unitary representation of the Poincare group, labelled by mass and spin (or helicity for m=0); spinor-helicity and little-group scaling in modern amplitudes are the same construction.
map: P^\mu P_\mu=-m^2c^2,\ W^\mu W_\mu=m^2c^2\hbar^2s(s+1);\quad m=0:\ \text{little group }ISO(2)\Rightarrow h=\pm s

name: Invariant mass and collider kinematics
summary: Collider physics runs on four-momentum invariants: resonance discovery by invariant-mass peaks, sqrt(s) of colliding beams versus fixed targets, rapidity and transverse momentum as boost-friendly variables, and partonic s-hat = x1 x2 s.

name: Neutrino speed bounds and the OPERA error
summary: Neutrino time of flight from SN1987A and long-baseline beams bounds |v-c|/c; the 2011 OPERA superluminal claim was traced to a faulty fibre connection, and superluminal neutrinos would lose energy by e+e- pair emission.

name: BBN constrains G and extra gravitational fields
summary: The neutron-proton freeze-out temperature depends on the expansion rate H proportional to sqrt(G rho); primordial helium and deuterium bound any change of G between BBN and today to roughly 10-20% and limit scalar-tensor and extra-radiation models.

name: Mossbauer gamma lines measured gravitational redshift
summary: Pound and Rebka resolved a fractional shift of 2.5e-15 over 22.5 m by using the recoil-free 14.4 keV nuclear gamma transition of Fe-57, whose natural linewidth made the nuclear transition a clock fine enough to see gravity.

name: Love numbers enter the 5PN waveform phase
summary: The quadrupole induced by the companion's tidal field, Q = -lambda E, adds a term scaling as Lambda (v/c)^10 to the inspiral phase; computing k_2 needs a perturbed TOV solution, so EOS physics enters waveform models directly.

name: Tidal deformability from GW170817
summary: Tidal deformation of inspiralling neutron stars shifts the GW phase; GW170817 bounded the combined tidal deformability and hence radii near 11-13 km, excluding the stiffest nuclear equations of state.

name: GW170817 kilonova as an r-process site
summary: The GW-localized merger GW170817 produced a kilonova whose red, lanthanide-rich emission powered by r-process decay showed that neutron-star mergers make heavy elements, tying nuclear masses and beta rates to GW sources.
map: L(t)\propto M_{\rm ej}\,\dot\epsilon(t),\ \dot\epsilon\propto t^{-1.3};\quad M_{\rm ej}\sim0.05\,M_\odot

name: BBN bound on primordial GW backgrounds
summary: Any primordial GW background present before BBN is extra radiation and raises N_eff; the light-element abundances cap its integrated energy density, a benchmark that LISA and PTA cosmological interpretations must respect.

name: eta/s = 1/4pi from black-brane horizons
summary: Shear viscosity of a strongly coupled plasma equals the absorption of gravitons by a black-brane horizon; for every two-derivative gravity dual eta/s = hbar/4pi k_B, close to the small eta/s extracted from RHIC/LHC flow.
breaks: N=4 SYM is conformal, supersymmetric and large-N; QCD near T_c is none of these, and the 1/4pi value is violated by higher-curvature corrections.

name: Hadronization as Unruh radiation
summary: Thermal hadron yields with a universal T near 160 MeV in e+e-, pp and AA have been modelled as Unruh radiation from quarks decelerated by the string tension at a confinement horizon, with T = a/2π and a ≃ √(2πσ), so T ≃ √(σ/2π) ≈ 160–180 MeV.
breaks: The confinement 'horizon' is not a spacetime horizon; universal thermal yields also follow from statistical hadronization without any Unruh mechanism.

name: Q-values and the direct test of E=mc^2
summary: Nuclear reaction energetics are mass-energy equivalence in action: Q = (sum m_i - sum m_f)c^2; comparing neutron-capture gamma energies with Penning-trap mass differences verified E=mc^2 to 4e-7.

name: Hughes-Drever tests with nuclear spins
summary: Hughes–Drever experiments look for sidereal variation of the quadrupole-split NMR or Zeeman spectrum of nuclei with J>1/2 (7Li, 21Ne, 133Cs, 201Hg). Shell-model wavefunctions convert the null results into limits on proton and neutron SME coefficients near 1e-30 GeV.
breaks: Interpreting a bound requires a nuclear model of which nucleons carry the spin, adding model dependence.

name: Area laws: black-hole and entanglement entropy
summary: Entanglement entropy of a field across a surface scales with its area, as does Bekenstein-Hawking entropy; in gapped topological phases the area law has a universal constant correction -gamma = -ln D, the same diagnostic used for long-range entanglement.
map: S_{\rm ent}=\alpha\frac{A}{\epsilon^{d-1}}+\dots\ (d\ \text{space dims});\ \ S=\alpha\frac{L}{\epsilon}-\gamma,\ \gamma=\ln\mathcal D\ (2+1\text{D});\ \leftrightarrow\ S_{\rm BH}=\frac{k_BA}{4\ell_P^2}
breaks: The entanglement coefficient alpha is cutoff-dependent; matching 1/4G needs renormalization of Newton's constant, while gamma has no BH counterpart.

name: SYK: strange metal and near-extremal black hole
summary: The Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model of randomly interacting fermions, rooted in a random-magnet spin fluid, has an extensive zero-temperature entropy and emergent reparametrization symmetry matching near-extremal charged black holes and JT gravity in AdS2; it also maximizes chaos.
breaks: Match holds only in the low-energy Schwarzian sector at large N; SYK is non-local and has no full gravity dual.

name: Gravity Probe B gyroscopes read by SQUIDs
summary: Gravity Probe B measured geodetic and frame-dragging precession of niobium-coated quartz rotors through the London moment of the spinning superconductor, read out by SQUID magnetometers at milliarcsecond resolution.

name: Amorphous mirror coatings limit LIGO thermal noise
summary: Around 50–300 Hz, Brownian thermal noise of the amorphous Ta2O5/SiO2 mirror coatings is one of LIGO's dominant limits, alongside quantum noise. Through fluctuation–dissipation (Levin's method) it is set by the coatings' mechanical loss angle, which is attributed to two-level systems in the glass.
map: S_x(f)=\frac{2k_BT}{\pi^2f^2}\frac{W_{\rm diss}}{F_0^2},\quad W_{\rm diss}\propto\phi_{\rm coat}\ (\text{loss angle})

name: Cryogenic crystalline test masses
summary: KAGRA uses 20 K sapphire and Einstein Telescope/LIGO Voyager plan cryogenic silicon test masses, chosen for low phonon loss and for silicon's vanishing thermal expansion near 123 K, which kills thermoelastic noise.

name: Dirac-fluid hydrodynamics near the KSS bound
summary: Near neutrality graphene electrons form a Dirac fluid described by relativistic hydrodynamics (as for the QGP) with small eta/s and violated Wiedemann-Franz; holographic models are used only as strong-coupling guides.
breaks: Graphene's coupling α_g≈0.5–2.2 flows logarithmically to weak coupling, so it is not a large-N strongly coupled CFT. Disorder and phonons matter, and no gravity dual is known.

name: Emergent gauge fields and gravity from many-body order
summary: String-net condensation in lattice spin models gives emergent photons and fermions, raising the question of whether gravity can emerge the same way; emergent-gravity programmes (Volovik, Wen) use topological order as a template.
breaks: Weinberg-Witten forbids a massless spin-2 particle from a Lorentz-covariant conserved stress tensor, and emergent Lorentz invariance is not exact on a lattice; no model yields Einstein gravity.

name: Spin-orbit coupling and Thomas precession
summary: An electron moving through an electric field sees B' = −v×E/c² in its rest frame, and Thomas precession halves the naive coupling to give the Pauli spin–orbit term. In solids this Dirac-equation term is greatly enhanced near heavy nuclei and by band structure, and it underlies the Rashba, Dresselhaus and spin Hall effects used in spintronics.

name: Stellar-mass black holes as end states of collapse
summary: Above the maximum neutron-star mass (~2.2–2.3 M_sun for cold, slowly rotating stars) no known pressure halts collapse, so heavier remnants become Kerr black holes. X-ray binaries such as Cyg X-1 provide measured masses and ISCO-based spins. The putative 2–5 M_sun lower mass gap is now challenged by GW190814 and GW230529.

name: M87*: horizon-scale image of an AGN engine
summary: The EHT image of M87*, the core of a radio-loud AGN with a kiloparsec jet, shows a ~42 μas ring that matches the Kerr shadow of a 6.5×10⁹ M_sun black hole. GRMHD accretion and jet models are scored directly against the image and its polarisation.

name: Sgr A*: the Galactic Centre black hole
summary: Decades of S-star orbits weigh Sgr A* at ~4×10⁶ M_sun, and in 2022 the EHT imaged it as a ~52 μas ring consistent with a Kerr shadow. The two methods give independent mass-to-distance ratios, and they agree.

name: de Sitter horizon thermodynamics
summary: In a Λ-dominated universe each observer has a cosmological event horizon. By the same surface-gravity mechanism as a black-hole horizon, it radiates at the Gibbons–Hawking temperature ħH/(2πk_B) and carries an area entropy. Its first law has the opposite sign, though, and the entropy's statistical meaning is debated. For our Λ, T~10⁻³⁰ K and S~10¹²² k_B, conjectured to be the maximum entropy accessible to an observer.
map: T_{\rm dS}=\frac{\hbar H}{2\pi k_B},\quad S_{\rm dS}=\frac{k_BA}{4\ell_P^2}=\frac{\pi k_Bc^5}{G\hbar H^2}
breaks: Our universe is only asymptotically de Sitter; quoted T and S use H₀ rather than the asymptotic H_Λ, and the maximum-entropy reading is heuristic.

name: Hawking evaporation bounds primordial-black-hole DM
summary: Primordial black holes lighter than ~5×10¹¹ kg would have evaporated by today, and slightly heavier ones would still emit Hawking gamma rays and e±. Gamma-ray, 511 keV-line and CMB data therefore exclude PBHs as all of the dark matter below ~10¹⁴ kg, leaving the asteroid-mass window open.

name: ISCO sets the radiative efficiency of accretion
summary: A thin accretion disk radiates the binding energy at the innermost stable circular orbit. Its efficiency η=1−E_ISCO rises from 5.7% for Schwarzschild (r=6GM/c²) to 42% for maximal prograde Kerr. Soltan's argument, comparing integrated quasar light with the relic SMBH mass density, uses η to infer typical spins.

name: Starobinsky R² inflation is f(R) gravity
summary: The action f(R)=R+R²/(6M²) is conformally equivalent (Einstein frame) to GR plus a scalar field with a plateau potential. Starobinsky's 1980 model, one of the earliest inflationary scenarios, predicts n_s≈1−2/N and r≈12/N², inside Planck's preferred region.

name: MOND needs a relativistic modified-gravity completion
summary: MOND modifies Newtonian dynamics below a₀≈1.2×10⁻¹⁰ m s⁻². To predict lensing and the CMB it needs a relativistic completion such as TeVeS or AeST, which places it among scalar–vector–tensor modified-gravity theories. GW170817 falsified the original TeVeS, which had gravitons and photons travelling on different metrics.

name: GW170817's speed of gravity prunes dark-energy models
summary: The 1.7 s delay between GW170817 and GRB 170817A over ~40 Mpc fixes the speed of gravity to within ~10⁻¹⁵ of c. This eliminates Horndeski and beyond-Horndeski dark-energy models whose tensor speed differs from c on cosmological backgrounds, including quartic and quintic galileons. The caveat is that the bound applies at LIGO frequencies, which de Rham and Melville noted lie near these theories' cutoff.

name: S2's orbit tests GR near Sgr A*
summary: Adaptive-optics astrometry and spectroscopy of the star S2 detected the combined gravitational redshift and transverse Doppler shift at its 2018 pericentre, and later the prograde Schwarzschild precession of its orbit. This carries tests of GR to the potential of a 4×10⁶ M_sun black hole.

name: Solar-System ephemerides as tests of GR
summary: Mercury's anomalous 43″ per century perihelion advance was GR's first success. Modern ephemerides, built from radar, spacecraft tracking and lunar laser ranging, must include 1PN terms; fits bound β to ~10⁻⁴ (γ ~10⁻⁵ with Cassini) and constrain the Nordtvedt effect and Ġ/G.
